title: Auto MPG · UCI
description: Estimate a vehicle model fuel efficiency (miles per gallon) from its technical characteristics.

dataset.name: Auto MPG · UCI
transformations: auto-mpg.data extracted unchanged from the official archive.
Missing horsepower (?) replaced by the training median in prepare_auto_mpg.py.
origin converted to indicator variables for codes 2 and 3.

facts.label: Cible
facts.value: mpg: city-cycle fuel efficiency in miles per gallon according to the source

facts.label: Observation unit
facts.value: A vehicle model for a model year
facts.source: Inspection: documentation describes unique names, but some recur across years

facts.label: Intended use
facts.value: Exercise: estimate a future model fuel efficiency from technical characteristics

facts.label: Decision studied
facts.value: Compare estimation methods without a real decision

facts.label: Prediction time
facts.value: When technical characteristics are fixed, before measuring fuel efficiency

facts.label: Repeated or temporal observations
facts.value: Model years 1970–1982; {{x:shared_names.count}} names occur on both sides of the split

facts.label: Meaning of origin codes
facts.value: Codes 1, 2, 3 are not documented in auto-mpg.names (often interpreted as USA, Europe, Japan)

variables.name: mpg
variables.label: Fuel efficiency (mpg)
variables.description: Miles per gallon: higher values mean lower fuel consumption.

variables.name: acceleration
variables.label: Acceleration
variables.description: Acceleration time; not used by models in this exercise.

variables.name: car_name
variables.label: Name
variables.description: Model name; an identifier, not used for estimation.

constraints: No new training from the companion.
limitations: Historical cars: a real-data exercise, not an estimate for a current vehicle.
ai_guidance: Express all errors in mpg (miles per gallon); higher mpg means lower fuel consumption.
Units marked assumed are undocumented: mention this when relevant to the answer.

start.title: Starting point
start.objective: Discover the cars, mpg target, and missing values.
start.lead: Can a vehicle model fuel efficiency be estimated from its characteristics?

blocks.title: What does a row look like?
blocks.intro: Six training cars from different years.

blocks.title: Understand features, units, and their status

use.title: What we estimate
use.objective: Connect estimation to its use and when characteristics are known.

blocks.question: What are we estimating, and when?

options.label: A model fuel efficiency in mpg from characteristics known before measurement
options.feedback: Yes. The target is numeric: discuss error in mpg, not correct or incorrect answers.

options.label: Whether a car is fuel-efficient
options.feedback: That is a different question requiring a category definition. Here the target is the mpg value itself.

protocol.title: Split by year
protocol.objective: Understand why the protocol is chronological rather than random.
protocol.lead: Learn from the past and compare on later years.

blocks.label: The protocol
blocks.text: {{p:chronological-70-78-vs-79-82.train}} cars from 1970–1978 for training and {{p:chronological-70-78-vs-79-82.validation}} cars from 1979–1982 for comparison. A random split would let the model train on years later than those it evaluates.

blocks.note: Same model, two protocols. The difference does not make random splitting better: it measures an easier situation than the intended one.

blocks.question: Why is error lower with the random split?

options.label: It mixes years: the model sees cars similar to those it evaluates
options.feedback: Yes. More recent cars consume less fuel; including them in training makes the comparison optimistic.

options.label: The model is better under this protocol
options.feedback: The model is the same. Only evaluation difficulty changes.

baseline.title: A simple reference
baseline.objective: Interpret mean absolute error in mpg relative to a reference.
baseline.lead: Read error in the target unit.

blocks.question: What does an MAE of {{r:linear-all.mae_mpg}} mean?

options.label: On average, estimates differ from observed efficiency by this amount
options.feedback: Yes. It is an average difference in mpg without indicating error direction.

options.label: The model is wrong on this proportion of cases
options.feedback: No: MAE is not a proportion of cases; it is an error in the target unit.

compare.title: Choose a model to examine
compare.objective: Choose an available model whose errors will be examined.

blocks.note: Models were trained once by prepare_auto_mpg.py; the companion only selects an existing result.

errors.title: Where are the errors?
errors.objective: Examine error by model year in the target unit.

blocks.title: Mean absolute error by validation year

blocks.label: What to observe
blocks.text: Mean signed error is negative: models underestimate mpg for newer, more fuel-efficient cars. This describes a difference without establishing its cause.

handoff.title: Review and hand over
handoff.lead: Assess an estimate in its unit and under an appropriate protocol.
